## Public reference pages
- https://theindustryguides.com/ — The Industry Guides | Source-Backed Guides and Provider Routing — Source-backed guides, state pages, comparisons, and provider routing across USCIS medical exams, personal injury, dentistry, neuropsych testing, hormones, IV and hair, and Memphis-area senior living.
- https://theindustryguides.com/about.html — About The Industry Guides and Its Editorial Team — About The Industry Guides: who publishes it, its editorial ownership, the evidence standards it holds to, and its provider-routing boundaries.
- https://theindustryguides.com/adhd-evaluation-vs-neuropsychological-evaluation/ — ADHD evaluation vs neuropsychological evaluation — An ADHD evaluation answers a focused diagnostic question; a neuropsychological evaluation is broader and may be useful when learning, memory, neurological, or complex differential questions are also present. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to neuroevalguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/atlas/ — Atlas: Every Vertical, Cluster and Question Page — Structured coverage map of every vertical, cluster, and mapped query page on The Industry Guides: Personal Injury, Dentistry, TRT & Hair, Neuropsych Evaluations, USCIS Medical Exams, Senior Living.
- https://theindustryguides.com/civil-surgeon-vs-panel-physician/ — Civil surgeon vs panel physician — Use a civil surgeon for USCIS adjustment-of-status medical exams in the United States; panel physicians handle immigration medical exams abroad under Department of State processes. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to uscisexam.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/comparative-negligence-vs-contributory-negligence/ — Comparative negligence vs contributory negligence — Comparative negligence reduces recovery according to assigned fault under state rules; contributory-negligence systems can bar recovery when the claimant is legally at fault, subject to jurisdiction-specific exceptions. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to theaccidentguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/cosmetic-vs-general-dentistry/ — Cosmetic dentistry vs general dentistry — General dentistry focuses on prevention, diagnosis, and oral health treatment; cosmetic dentistry focuses on appearance, although many procedures overlap and still require clinical assessment. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to dentistryguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dental-implant-vs-bridge-vs-denture/ — Dental implant vs bridge vs denture — Implants, bridges, and dentures replace missing teeth in different ways. Compare candidacy, adjacent-tooth impact, surgery, maintenance, timeline, and total cost rather than choosing by price alone. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to dentistryguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dental-insurance-vs-medical-insurance/ — Dental insurance vs medical insurance — Dental and medical plans use different benefit designs, networks, exclusions, and claim rules. A service involving the mouth is not automatically covered by dental insurance, and medical coverage is not automatic either. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to dentistryguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dentist-vs-oral-surgeon-vs-endodontist/ — Dentist vs oral surgeon vs endodontist — A general dentist manages broad oral care, an oral surgeon handles surgical conditions, and an endodontist focuses on dental pulp and root-canal treatment. The diagnosis determines the right provider. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to dentistryguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dentistry/ — Dentistry Atlas (Quick Answers) — A neutral dentistry decision guide for comparing cost, insurance, anxiety, sedation, pediatric, implant, and second-opinion questions before booking care.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dentistry/dental-school-clinics/ — Dental School Clinic Near Me: Reduced-Fee Care From Supervised Students — A dental school clinic treats the public at reduced fees: dental students and residents provide care under the close supervision of licensed dentists, and dental hygiene programs offer supervised cleanings, X-rays and preventive care. Find accredited programs near you in the Commission on Dental Accreditation directory, and expect a screening visit first, longer appointments and several visits.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dentistry/free-dental-clinics/ — Free Dental Clinics Near Me: How to Find Free and Low-Cost Dental Care — A free or low-cost dental clinic near you is one of three kinds: a federally funded community health center that charges on a sliding scale by income, a public health department dental clinic, or a volunteer charity clinic. Find community health centers with HRSA's Find a Health Center search, then call to confirm eligibility, documents and cost before you go.
- https://theindustryguides.com/dentistry/states/connecticut/medicaid-dental-coverage/ — Connecticut Medicaid Dental Coverage Guide — Connecticut Medicaid Dental Coverage Guide: verify the Connecticut authority path, document the current rule or credential, compare written provider terms, and continue through Find a Provider only after the evidence check.

- https://theindustryguides.com/i-693-rejection-vs-denial-vs-rfe/ — I-693 rejection vs denial vs RFE — A rejection usually means a filing was returned before adjudication, an RFE requests missing evidence during review, and a denial is an unfavorable adjudication. The response path depends on the notice. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to uscisexam.com for the complete canonical next step.
